description: Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) parameters for hydrogen vs. diesel Class 8 trucks in California

diesel_tco_usd_per_mile.description: ATRI motor carrier cost data (USD/mile), held constant across all years
diesel_tco_usd_per_mile.source: American Transportation Research Institute, An Analysis of the Operational Costs of Trucking: 2026 Update
diesel_tco_usd_per_mile.comment_driver_and_other: Driver wages, benefits, tolls, permits & licenses and insurance, reported as a single line in the source table. Assumed identical for hydrogen trucks — see identical_cost_categories.
diesel_tco_usd_per_mile.comment_total: Reference value from the source table; the model sums the components rather than reading this field.
diesel_tco_usd_per_mile.comment_miles_per_gallon: Class 8 fleet-average diesel fuel economy. Single source of truth: the figures read it via TCO_DIESEL_MPG in figures/config_defaults.jl. Used to convert a pump price ($/gal) into a fuel cost ($/mile) and to express the LCFS credit/deficit per mile.
diesel_tco_usd_per_mile.comment_fuel_line_item: The 'fuel' figure above is ATRI's reported national-average fuel cost ($0.482/mile, i.e. $3.58/gal at 7.43 mpg). The figures do NOT use it as the diesel reference — they use the California pump-price scenarios below. It is retained because it belongs to the ATRI cost table.

diesel_price_usd_per_gallon.description: California retail diesel pump-price scenarios used as the fuel reference in every figure. Single source of truth: read via TCO_DIESEL_P_LO / TCO_DIESEL_P_HI in figures/config_defaults.jl — never hard-code these.
diesel_price_usd_per_gallon.comment_basis: Both are 2026 prices. Figures hold them flat in real terms and apply only the LCFS credit/deficit change over time; they are deliberately above ATRI's national-average fuel line item, which is not a California pump price.

hydrogen_truck.description: Capital cost and drivetrain assumptions for Class 8 hydrogen fuel cell trucks
hydrogen_truck.comment_subsidy: California HVIP subsidy — initial value (2026). See subsidy_schedule for phase-out.
hydrogen_truck.comment_net_cost: Net cost at 2026 (purchase - subsidy). Decreases as subsidy phases out.
hydrogen_truck.comment_subsidy_schedule: HVIP subsidy phase-out. Value steps down at each listed year. Edit years/amounts here to change the phase-out trajectory.
hydrogen_truck.comment_lifetime: Truck lifetime for annualization matches the operational lifetime used in the model (7 years)
hydrogen_truck.comment_mileage: Fuel economy in miles per kg H2. Derives annual mileage via h2_per_truck_per_day × operating_days_per_year from model_defaults.json: 38 × 250 × 9 = 85,500 miles/truck/year. Note the annual mileage used for per-mile TCO does NOT apply the fleet utilization ramp — it is the full-utilization figure, consistent with the model's demand basis from 2028 onward (utilization = 1.00).
hydrogen_truck.comment_rm: 2× diesel R&M reflecting higher service costs during early commercialization
hydrogen_truck.comment_tires: 1.5× diesel tires reflecting heavier fuel cell system / hydrogen storage weight
hydrogen_truck.comment_platform: Mature truck platform (chassis, cab, axles) — not subject to learning rate reductions

learning.description: Wright's Law cost reduction applied to fuel cell system cost only (not platform). Driven by global cumulative H2 truck fleet stock. Same functional form as electrolyzer/solar CAPEX learning in the main model.
learning.comment_lr: 15% cost reduction per doubling of cumulative global H2 truck fleet stock
learning.comment_reference: Fuel cell system cost of 260,000 USD applies at this reference year
learning.comment_observed: Global cumulative H2 truck fleet stock (vehicles). 2025 is full-year estimate. Source: IEA Global Hydrogen Review 2025.
learning.projection_method: Cubic OLS fit (Vandermonde matrix) to observed fleet stock data, extended through 2040. Implemented in fig_tco_comparison.jl. Fleet stock used directly as the Wright's Law cumulative production driver.

identical_cost_categories.description: Cost categories assumed identical between diesel and hydrogen trucks (USD/mile, from ATRI 2026 Update). Driver wages, benefits, tolls, permits & licenses and insurance are reported as one line in the source table and are carried as a single aggregate.
